# Linear programming for complex balanced and detailed balanced realizations of reaction networks

**Setting.** A mass-action kinetic system $\dot x = M\psi(x)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}$ (a *kinetic polynomial system*, with monomial vector $\psi$ and coefficient matrix $M$) can be generated by many reaction networks. A *realization* is a pair $(Y, A_k)$: $Y \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^{n\times m}$ lists complex compositions, $\psi_j(x) = \prod_i x_i^{Y_{ij}}$, and $A_k$ is a Kirchhoff matrix (nonnegative off-diagonal entries $a_{ij}$ = rate constant of reaction $C_j \to C_i$, zero column sums), with $\dot x = Y A_k\psi(x)$. Reversibility, weak reversibility, deficiency, complex balance and detailed balance are properties of realizations, not of the ODE, yet they imply stability results (e.g. the deficiency-zero theorem).

**Definitions.** $(Y, A_k)$ is *complex balanced* at $x^* > 0$ if $A_k\psi(x^*) = 0$, and *detailed balanced* at $x^*$ if it is reversible and $a_{ij}\psi_j(x^*) = a_{ji}\psi_i(x^*)$ for every reversible pair, equivalently $GA_k^{\mathsf T} = A_kG$ with $G = \mathrm{diag}(\psi(x^*))$.

**Linear-programming characterisation.** Fix the complex set $Y$ (e.g. all monomials of $M$) and a positive steady state $x^*$. Collect the unknown Kirchhoff entries columnwise into $y = (a_{11}, a_{21}, \dots, a_{mm})^{\mathsf T} \ge 0$ (diagonal entries entered with a negative sign). Then:
1. *Dynamical equivalence* ($YA_k = M$ with zero column sums of $A_k$) is the linear system $A_{e1}y = B_{e1}$, block diagonal with blocks $\bar Y^i = \begin{pmatrix}Y_{\cdot,1} & \cdots & -Y_{\cdot,i} & \cdots & Y_{\cdot,m}\\ 1 & \cdots & -1 & \cdots & 1\end{pmatrix}$ and right-hand side the columns of $M$ padded with $0$.
2. *Complex balance at $x^*$* adds the linear constraints $\sum_j a_{ij}\psi_j(x^*) - a_{ii}\psi_i(x^*) = 0$ for each complex $i$.
3. *Detailed balance at $x^*$* adds $\psi_i(x^*)\,a_{ji} - \psi_j(x^*)\,a_{ij} = 0$ for all $i > j$, which also forces reversibility.

Hence a complex (detailed) balanced realization with the given complexes exists iff the corresponding LP is feasible, which is decided in polynomial time by the auxiliary problem $\min\sum_i z_i$ subject to $Ay + z = b$, $y, z \ge 0$ (with $b \ge 0$): the LP is feasible iff this minimum is $0$. A linear objective (e.g. minimising or maximising $\sum a_{ij}$) selects sparse or dense realizations, and one network can admit several distinct detailed balanced realizations.

## Proof sketch

Because $x^*$ is fixed, every condition in the definitions is linear in the rate constants: dynamical equivalence matches coefficients of each monomial, complex balance is flux conservation at each complex evaluated at the known monomial values, and detailed balance equates forward and reverse fluxes pairwise. A complex balanced realization of a kinetic system has every positive steady state complex balanced, hence a unique locally asymptotically stable positive equilibrium in each stoichiometric class with a Lyapunov function; detailed balanced realizations give thermodynamically consistent reversible models. The search therefore replaces combinatorial enumeration of network structures by a single LP.
